e-12442.problem: Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through $P(3,-1,7)$ and parallel to ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073156/assets/48f9afd751f6424fe465e494fd254593de065563231a1f5df07741789969c1af.png)
e-12442.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $P$ and parallel to $\mathbf{v}$ is given by

$$
\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{p} + t \mathbf{v},
$$

where $t \in (-\infty, \infty)$ and $\mathbf{p}$ is the position vector of $P$.

In our case, the position vector of the point $P$ is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073156/assets/9264ecd5e62e51eec08ae686461f8b3d99aadbddd2363b5c700c72839d59524f.png)

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

e-12443.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Equation of the Line Passing Through Two Given Points
e-12443.problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $P(1,-1,2)$ and $Q(3,2,7).$
e-12443.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $P$ and parallel to $\mathbf{v}$ is given by

$$
\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{p} + t \mathbf{v},
$$

where $t \in (-\infty, \infty)$ and $\mathbf{p}$ is the position vector of $P.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $P(1,-1,2)$ and $Q(3,2,7),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =⟨3,2,7⟩-⟨1,-1,2⟩ \\  & =⟨2,3,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through P(−3,−4,−5) and parallel to v=[1−1−2].

a
r=[−3−4−5]+[1−1−2]
b
r=[1−1−2]+t[−3−4−5],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[−21−1]+t[−5−4−3],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[−3−4−5]+t[1−1−2],t∈(−∞,∞)
e

decision.explanation: A line through P with direction v has equation r=p+tv. Option d uses p=(-3,-4,-5) and v=(1,-1,-2); at t=0 it passes through P, and its direction is v.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through $P(-3,-4,-5)$ and parallel to $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $P$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=p+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

In our case, the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -4 \\ -5\end{aligned}].$

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through P(−3,−4,−5) and parallel to v=[1−1−2].

a
r=[−3−4−5]+[1−1−2]
b
r=[1−1−2]+t[−3−4−5],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[−21−1]+t[−5−4−3],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[−3−4−5]+t[1−1−2],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[−3−5−4]+t[1−2−1],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The vector equation of the straight line passing through P and parallel to v is given by r=p+tv,

where t∈(−∞,∞) and p is the position vector of P.

In our case, the position vector of the point P is p=[−3−4−5].

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

r=[−3−4−5]+t[1−1−2],t∈(−∞,∞).

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Equation of a Line Given a Point and Direction Vector
content.problem: Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through $P(-3,-4,-5)$ and parallel to $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $P$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=p+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

In our case, the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -4 \\ -5\end{aligned}].$

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through Q(−3,3,3) and parallel to v=⟨23,−5,3⟩.

a
r=⟨−3,3,3⟩+t⟨23,−5,3⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=⟨23,−5,3⟩+t⟨−3,3,3⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=⟨−3,3,3⟩+⟨23,−5,3⟩
d
r=⟨−5,3,23⟩+t⟨3,3,−3⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=⟨3,−3,3⟩+t⟨23,3,−5⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: The line has equation r=q+tv. Option a uses q=⟨-3,3,3⟩, so t=0 gives Q, and its direction vector is the given v=⟨√2/3,-5,3⟩.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through $Q(-3,3,3)$ and parallel to $v=⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},-5,3⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $Q$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=q+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $q$ is the position vector of $Q.$

In our case, the position vector of the point $Q$ is $q=⟨-3,3,3⟩.$

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨-3,3,3⟩+t⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},-5,3⟩,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through Q(−3,3,3) and parallel to v=⟨23,−5,3⟩.

a
r=⟨−3,3,3⟩+t⟨23,−5,3⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=⟨23,−5,3⟩+t⟨−3,3,3⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=⟨−3,3,3⟩+⟨23,−5,3⟩
d
r=⟨−5,3,23⟩+t⟨3,3,−3⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=⟨3,−3,3⟩+t⟨23,3,−5⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The vector equation of the straight line passing through Q and parallel to v is given by r=q+tv,

where t∈(−∞,∞) and q is the position vector of Q.

In our case, the position vector of the point Q is q=⟨−3,3,3⟩.

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

r=⟨−3,3,3⟩+t⟨23,−5,3⟩,t∈(−∞,∞).

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option a: r=q+tv passes through Q at t=0 and has the specified direction vector. Option c omits the parameter and describes only one point, not a line.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Equation of a Line Given a Point and Direction Vector
content.problem: Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through $Q(-3,3,3)$ and parallel to $v=⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},-5,3⟩.$
content.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $Q$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=q+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $q$ is the position vector of $Q.$

In our case, the position vector of the point $Q$ is $q=⟨-3,3,3⟩.$

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨-3,3,3⟩+t⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},-5,3⟩,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through P(−1,−4,5) and parallel to v=[10−1].

a
r=[10−1]+t[−1−45],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[−1−45]+t[10−1],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[1−10]+t[5−4−1],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[−1−45]+[1−10]
e
r=[−1−45]+t[1−10],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: Use r=p+tv with p=(-1,-4,5) and v=(1,0,-1). Option b passes through P at t=0 and has the required direction vector.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through $P(-1,-4,5)$ and parallel to $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $P$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=p+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

In our case, the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through P(−1,−4,5) and parallel to v=[10−1].

a
r=[10−1]+t[−1−45],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[−1−45]+t[10−1],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[1−10]+t[5−4−1],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[−1−45]+[1−10]
e
r=[−1−45]+t[1−10],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The vector equation of the straight line passing through P and parallel to v is given by r=p+tv,

where t∈(−∞,∞) and p is the position vector of P.

In our case, the position vector of the point P is p=[−1−45].

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

r=[−1−45]+t[10−1],t∈(−∞,∞).

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Equation of a Line Given a Point and Direction Vector
content.problem: Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through $P(-1,-4,5)$ and parallel to $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $P$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=p+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

In our case, the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: A line through Q parallel to v has equation r=q+tv. Option a uses Q's position vector and the given direction v, so it passes through Q at t=0 and is parallel to v.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through $Q(\sqrt{5},\,\frac{3}{5},\,-2)$ and parallel to $v=⟨2,\,3,\,-1⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $Q$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=q+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $q$ is the position vector of $Q.$ 

In our case, the position vector of the point $Q$ is $q=⟨\sqrt{5},\,\frac{3}{5},\,-2⟩.$ 

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

$$
r=⟨\sqrt{5},\,\frac{3}{5},\,-2⟩+t⟨2,\,3,\,-1⟩,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through Q(5,35,−2) and parallel to v=⟨2,3,−1⟩.

a
r=⟨5,35,−2⟩+t⟨2,3,−1⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=⟨2,−1,3⟩+t⟨5,−2,35⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=⟨−2,35,5⟩+t⟨−1,2,3⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=⟨2,3,−1⟩+⟨5,35,−2⟩
e
r=⟨2,3,−1⟩+t⟨5,35,−2⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The vector equation of the straight line passing through Q and parallel to v is given by r=q+tv,

where t∈(−∞,∞) and q is the position vector of Q.

In our case, the position vector of the point Q is q=⟨5,35,−2⟩.

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

r=⟨5,35,−2⟩+t⟨2,3,−1⟩,t∈(−∞,∞).

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option a. At t=0 it gives Q=(√5,3/5,-2), and its direction vector is (2,3,-1). Option c has direction (-1,2,3), which is not parallel to the given vector.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Equation of a Line Given a Point and Direction Vector
content.problem: Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through $Q(\sqrt{5},\,\frac{3}{5},\,-2)$ and parallel to $v=⟨2,\,3,\,-1⟩.$
content.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $Q$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=q+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $q$ is the position vector of $Q.$ 

In our case, the position vector of the point $Q$ is $q=⟨\sqrt{5},\,\frac{3}{5},\,-2⟩.$ 

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

$$
r=⟨\sqrt{5},\,\frac{3}{5},\,-2⟩+t⟨2,\,3,\,-1⟩,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Question 5
?

Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through P(5,5,−5) and parallel to v=⟨0,−5,−1⟩.

a
r=⟨−5,5,5⟩+t⟨−1,−5,0⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=⟨0,−1,−5⟩+t⟨5,−5,5⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=⟨0,−5,−1⟩+⟨5,5,−5⟩
d
r=⟨5,5,−5⟩+t⟨0,−5,−1⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=⟨0,−5,−1⟩+t⟨5,5,−5⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: Use r=p+tv. Option d has position vector p=⟨5,5,-5⟩ and direction v=⟨0,-√5,-1⟩, so it passes through P at t=0 and is parallel to v.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through $P(5,5,-5)$ and parallel to $v=⟨0,-\sqrt{5},-1⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $P$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=p+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

In our case, the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨5,5,-5⟩.$

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨5,5,-5⟩+t⟨0,-\sqrt{5},-1⟩,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through P(5,5,−5) and parallel to v=⟨0,−5,−1⟩.

a
r=⟨−5,5,5⟩+t⟨−1,−5,0⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=⟨0,−1,−5⟩+t⟨5,−5,5⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=⟨0,−5,−1⟩+⟨5,5,−5⟩
d
r=⟨5,5,−5⟩+t⟨0,−5,−1⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=⟨0,−5,−1⟩+t⟨5,5,−5⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The vector equation of the straight line passing through P and parallel to v is given by r=p+tv,

where t∈(−∞,∞) and p is the position vector of P.

In our case, the position vector of the point P is p=⟨5,5,−5⟩.

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

r=⟨5,5,−5⟩+t⟨0,−5,−1⟩,t∈(−∞,∞).

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Equation of a Line Given a Point and Direction Vector
content.problem: Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through $P(5,5,-5)$ and parallel to $v=⟨0,-\sqrt{5},-1⟩.$
content.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $P$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=p+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

In our case, the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨5,5,-5⟩.$

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨5,5,-5⟩+t⟨0,-\sqrt{5},-1⟩,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $H(5,7,2)$ and $S(3,4,5).$
after.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $H$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=h+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $h$ is the position vector of $H.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $H(5,7,2)$ and $S(3,4,5),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{HS} \\  & =⟨3,4,5⟩-⟨5,7,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,-3,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 7 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points H(5,7,2) and S(3,4,5).

a
r=[572]+t[2−32],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[250]+t[−2−33],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[345]+t[−23−3],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[572]+t[−2−33],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[−2−33]+t[572],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The vector equation of the straight line passing through H and parallel to v is given by r=h+tv, where t∈(−∞,∞) and h is the position vector of H.

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points H(5,7,2) and S(3,4,5), as follows:

v=HS→=⟨3,4,5⟩−⟨5,7,2⟩=⟨−2,−3,3⟩

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

r=[572]+t[−2−33],t∈(−∞,∞).

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option d: S−H=(-2,-3,3), so r=H+t(S−H) gives H at t=0 and S at t=1. Option b has the correct direction but lies on a different parallel line.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Equation of the Line Passing Through Two Given Points
content.problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $H(5,7,2)$ and $S(3,4,5).$
content.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $H$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=h+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $h$ is the position vector of $H.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $H(5,7,2)$ and $S(3,4,5),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{HS} \\  & =⟨3,4,5⟩-⟨5,7,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,-3,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 7 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: D−C=(2−3,1−2,6−5)=(-1,-1,1). Option a gives r=C+t(D−C), which passes through C at t=0 and D at t=1.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $C(3,2,5)$ and $D(2,1,6).$
after.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $C$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=c+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $c$ is the position vector of $C.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $C(3,2,5)$ and $D(2,1,6)$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{CD} \\  & =⟨2,1,6⟩-⟨3,2,5⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,-1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points C(3,2,5) and D(2,1,6).

a
r=[325]+t[−1−11],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[216]+t[1−11],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[325]+t[5311],t∈(−∞,∞)

r=[316]+t[−1−11],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[325]+t[1−1−1],t∈(−∞,∞)

Correct
EXPLANATION

The vector equation of the straight line passing through C and parallel to v is given by r=c+tv, where t∈(−∞,∞) and c is the position vector of C.

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points C(3,2,5) and D(2,1,6), as follows:

v=CD→=⟨2,1,6⟩−⟨3,2,5⟩=⟨−1,−1,1⟩

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

r=[325]+t[−1−11],t∈(−∞,∞).

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Equation of the Line Passing Through Two Given Points
content.problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $C(3,2,5)$ and $D(2,1,6).$
content.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $C$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=c+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $c$ is the position vector of $C.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $C(3,2,5)$ and $D(2,1,6)$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{CD} \\  & =⟨2,1,6⟩-⟨3,2,5⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,-1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
